   layouts S1, design S1, security S2, obs S1–S3).

     `"4x"` as a `u32`. On the `Err` it logs one `warn` under the crate's own target with:

     - a fixed message.

     that replays those steps also reads it: MCP in process, the session socket, the kept check and its replay.
     Assert first that the step caused exactly one item, an app `warn` record tied to the button's id
     (test-plan · decision/stand-checks-in-both-layout-modes).
   - The item's `error` field reads the literal `PARSE_ERROR` («invalid digit found in string», `:42`), already
     measured. `url` and `path` read `REDACTED`. Neither sentinel occurs in the written line, and the line writes
     `{"name":"error","value":"invalid digit found in string"}`.
   - The file's `//!` doc gains the sentence.

6. **The engine failure read from the answer and the sink** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_error_text.rs`.
   - Add an in-file failing network stand-in (a single reader, so it stays in the file, as `LateNet` does at
     `stand_load_wait.rs:50`). Its `fetch` answers every request at once through the handler's `error`, with a fixed
     text that holds the request's URL: the founder's stated price, a failed fetch's URL inside its error text.
   - Add a page with one button whose click links a stylesheet at a `.test` URL.
   - Add a hold that boots the page with `stand::options(incremental)` and that stand-in as `net_provider`, the
     pattern of `stand_load_wait.rs:63-70`, under the file's existing session label.

     failed stylesheet ends the load wait (test-plan · decision/failed-load-ends-settle-wait).

       stand-in's text and `url` reading `REDACTED`, with `waiting_nodes` whole;
     - on a build without it, no engine item, as the helper asserts today (test-plan ·
       decision/engine-items-asserted-on-tracing-build).

7. **The sink unchanged** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_error_text.rs`, the founder check
   `no_sentinel_payload_or_raw_href_reaches_the_sinks_lines` (`:852-905`). It already opens an empty capture before
   its sink (architecture · decision/capture-before-own-recorder).
   - Inside its `with_default`, it also runs step 6's click on a session of its own.
   - Its needles gain `PARSE_ERROR`, step 5's two sentinels and the stand-in's error text. Each occurs 0 times on the
     sink's lines on every build. The app record is dropped whole (`format.rs:99`), and the engine record's fields
     print redacted (`format.rs:101-106`).
   - On a build with the engine's tracing, the written lines also hold the engine record's line under a `blitz_dom`
     target. That line prints `error=[redacted]` and `url=[redacted]`, read through the same constant.
   - Failure messages name a mode, a build and an index alone (obs S3).
- none
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/capture.rs` — the answer's private set read by `Values::keep`; module and `KeptField` docs; the table unit test
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` — one test row pinning `error` redacted under an `escher_*` target
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — `caused`'s result-field help: `error` crosses as written
- `packages/escher-driver/src/caused.rs` — module doc and `fields` doc name the answer's own set
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_error_text.rs` — the app failure's step, the engine failure's test and stand-in, the sink check's needles and engine line
The gates are:
- escher-telemetry's and escher-driver's unit tests;
- the error-text target in both layout modes, package-alone (its engine branch reading no engine item);
- a probe that the help no longer lists `error` among the hidden names;
- then the pre-push gate and `stand-repeat`.

No boot-path touchpoint changes a binary's start. `host_log` and `mcp_log` drive both binaries' roles, and stand in
for the smoke. There is no live leg. The coverage leg is not listed: escher-driver's change is help and doc text, and
the capture code is escher-telemetry's, which has no floor.

Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S2). After the steps are green, /implement runs three one-shot
`gate.py control` runs, never entries:

- **`error` back in the answer's set** (`capture.rs`, the private constant gains `"error"`). Fired on the
  escher-telemetry unit entry, case: the table test of step 2. Fired again on the error-text entry, case: the test
  that runs `every_failure`, `each_failure_answers_what_failed_where_and_from_which_source`.

- **`error` out of the sink's set** (`format.rs`, `"error",` removed from `CONTENT_FIELDS`). Fired on the
  escher-telemetry unit entry, case: `content_fields_redact_for_any_target`. Its removal also opens `error` in the
  answer's set only if step 1 derived one set from the other, which step 1 forbids.

- **The capture judging by the sink's set again** (`capture.rs:276` restored to `CONTENT_FIELDS`). Fired on the
  tracing error-text entry, case: step 6's engine test.
Each control names the edit's text and the case by its test name (gate-contract.md §Control).

The diff is not OS-sensitive: no `cfg` site is added or changed, and the texts compared are a parse error's Display
and fixed strings. An acceptance reads CI, because the workspace test leg on linux, windows and macOS is where the
engine branch runs on every OS, and the socket case is unix-gated. So the operator's hygiene, push and CI entries
stand.

escher's telemetry bootstrap (unpublished, no `[features]`): one process-global stderr `tracing` subscriber that stamps the service identity on every line, applies a target allowlist in its formatter — it scrubs the records of engine and escher targets and drops every other target's — bridges `log` records and chains a panic hook; beside the sink it offers a scoped log capture, set by the driver around an acting step, which prints nothing and keeps the step's records and panics in process, a field of the answer's own hidden set reading `[redacted]`, an `error` field kept as written (cut at the text bound) and the message and other fields kept as written — the Dioxus framework targets (`dioxus*`, `generational_box`, `warnings`) and the engine targets only at warn and error, `escher_` targets never, every other outside target at every level, each kept text cut at 1024 bytes saying how much, at most 8 fields a record and 16 records a source kept and the rest counted. Not its job: OTel export (escher ships none — no OTel crate, no egress and no `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` credential path — ruled by the founder, 2026-10-06; the transport and credential path are a residual, `res-fzitzzw2` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next)), a log file or JSON schema, and the agent-run / cold-agent harness logs (harness metadata, not this sink) — though since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the cold-agent pipe spawns its live `escher-session mcp --record <abs target/cold-agent/record>` child with `RUST_LOG=info` set on that child only (its kept checks owner-only under `target/cold-agent/record/`, never printed or copied), so this sink's closed `tool_call` / `command` span lines land in `target/cold-agent/server.log`, which the pipe reads only to count ` span="tool_call" ` lines, their ` ending="refused" ` / ` ending="error" ` and the accepted lines of each counted verb (`lint` · `screenshot` · `advance`), never printing or copying it; its two replay children, spawned without `--record`, send stderr to `/dev/null`.

- `VERBS` — the verb table, fourteen verbs in three levels (`Level::Instance` · `Level::Session` · `Level::Tool`, the third since 2026-10-12-self-description): `snapshot` (one optional `part`; result `text`, then `part` and `parts`, two counts written only when the screen is read in parts), `click` (`id`), `type` (`id`, `text`), `press` (`key`, optional `shift`), `advance` (`ms`), `scroll` (`id`; the sixth, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07), `screenshot` (one optional `id`; result `width` (count), `height` (count) and `png` (`FieldKind::Png`, base64 text), all always present; the seventh, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, its help stating one measured limit — an element shot is cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — the overlay scrollbar fade reading the session's clock, so two shots of one state with no `advance` between them read the same pixels (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)), `lint` (the eighth, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: no argument, one named refused `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed`; result `findings`, `FieldKind::Entries`, always present; its help stating the six defect words, each reason's keys and its limits — geometry only, no hit, right-to-left and vertical text read as left-to-right lines), `graph` (the ninth, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: no argument, an argument refused `malformed` with nothing run; result `nodes` (`FieldKind::GraphNodes`) and `states` (`FieldKind::GraphStates`), the screen's UI graph read whole), `actions` (the tenth, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here: no argument, an argument refused `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed`; result `nodes` (`FieldKind::ActionNodes`), what each actionable node can take now, its help pinned word for word), then `start` (`app`), `status` and `stop` (session-level; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), then `help` (tool-level, no argument; result `verbs` · `node_keys` · `key_names` · `busy_classes` · `causes` · `exit_statuses` · `session_errors`, each field with its help; since 2026-10-12-self-description, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); each a `VerbSpec { name, level, help, args, fields }`; `verb(name)` finds one by its exact name only. Argument kinds and bounds (`ArgKind`): `id` 1 to `MAX_ID_BYTES` (1024) bytes of text · `text` 0 to `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (4096) bytes · `key` one of the twelve `KEY_NAMES` · `flag` · `milliseconds` 1 to `MAX_MILLISECONDS` (60000) · `name` 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` · `part` a whole number 1 to `MAX_PART` (1000), `snapshot`'s, the seventh kind. The acting verbs' result: `settled` (its help stating the load wait's bound, «a load in flight waited for up to 5 s», since 2026-10-20-load-wait), `busy` (one of `BUSY_CLASSES`, only when not settled), `added`, `removed`, `changed` (nodes carry the `NODE_FIELDS`), and, since 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action, `caused`, present only when the step caused something: an item per panic, error or record — its kind, level, source, target, message cut at 1024 bytes, location, an error's boundary and chain, a log's fields, its `error` field kept, and the first reached handler — panics, then errors new since the boundary marks, then records, 16 kept, and `caused_past`, written after `caused` only when non-empty, one entry per kind and source counting the items past `caused`'s 16, a panic or error entry writing no source; `advance` adds `advanced_ms`, `scroll` adds `in_view` (always present); `help`'s fields are of the kinds `Words` · `Entries`, and `screenshot`'s `png` of `Png` (base64 text, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) , and `graph`'s `nodes` and `states` of `GraphNodes` (`graph-nodes`) and `GraphStates` (`graph-states`), and `actions`' `nodes` of `ActionNodes` (`action-nodes`), sharing `graph`'s field name and not its kind — thirteen `FieldKind`s. Since 2026-10-12-self-description the command line's four exit statuses are the schema's `EXIT_STATUSES: [ExitStatus; 4]` (`ExitStatus { status, name, meaning }`: `0` `accepted` · `1` `refused` · `2` `usage` · `3` `session-error`), which the command line's status constants read and `help` serves, and `describe() -> String` writes the tool's self-description, `help`'s answer, as one line of JSON from the tables alone — 14 verbs, 14 node keys, 12 key names, 3 busy classes, 8 causes and 15 session errors with their remedies (13 until 2026-10-19-session-recording), 4 exit statuses — reading no environment and printing nothing; the command line's `help` and the MCP `help` tool serve the same bytes. The help of `changed` and of `snapshot`'s `text` say the state words and the two limits of the boolean model — a mixed toggle reads unpressed (`pressed` false), a grammar or spelling error reads invalid — so an agent learns them from the tool; since 2026-10-12-self-description `NODE_FIELDS` is `[NodeFieldSpec; 14]`, each row `NodeFieldSpec { name, help }` whose help states the key's reading — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's own state, else the toggle of the five checkable roles (`aria-checked`), a mixed one reading false, `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid` read by `aria-selected` · `aria-pressed` (left out for those five roles) · `aria-invalid`, the two limits among them — and the crate docs' one sentence says each limit is stated in its node key's help and that a changed node names the keys whose reading differs (`differs`).

- `command_line(args, apps, boot) -> ExitCode` — the whole command line of a binary that boots apps (`boot` an `FnMut` since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface); it installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable. The reader's rules, in order: no first word → usage; `serve <app> --session <dir>` in exactly that shape or with one `--record <dir>` after it, else usage; `mcp` alone or with one `--record <dir>`, else usage (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface; `--record` since 2026-10-19-session-recording); since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage `coverage <app> <check>...` in that one shape — an app the binary boots, then one or more kept-check paths, no `--session` and no `--record` word among them — else usage, each path read through `File::open(..).take(MAX_CHECK_BYTES + 1)`, then `Check::from_bytes`, a file that cannot be read, one past the bound, one that is no check and a check whose `app()` is not `<app>` refused `malformed`, status `1`, holding nothing of the path or the file, accepted the coverage line on stdout, status `0`, a boot that fails the session error, status `3`, the role calling the binary's boot once per check through `handler_coverage`; a `--record` anywhere else, twice or with no value is usage once the call passed `validate`; `help` with no argument and at most one `--session <dir>`, which is not read, answers `describe()`'s line on stdout, status `0`, reaching no session — `help` with an argument is refused `malformed`, `1`, and `--session` with no directory or given twice is usage, `2` (since 2026-10-12-self-description); a first word the verb table does not hold → the refusal `unknown-verb`; the call the remaining words spell (flags as the schema spells them — `--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` and `--part` each with one value, `--ms`'s and `--part`'s read as a number, `--shift` bare; `start`'s app as one plain word) is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for; then `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage; `start` on an app the binary does not boot → usage. Four endings: accepted — the answer on stdout, status `0`; refused — the refusal on stdout, `1`; usage — one fixed line on stderr built from `VERBS` and the app names, `2`; session error — the error object on stdout and its message on stderr, `3`; the host role ends quiet, status `0`; the `mcp` role hands stdin and stdout to `serve_mcp` with `IDLE_EXPIRY` and writes nothing on stdout at its end — `0` on `Ok`, `3` with the error's fixed message on stderr on `Err` — and the usage line names it (`; mcp role: mcp [--record <dir>]`, then `; coverage role: coverage <app> <check>...;` before `; apps:`), with `snapshot [--part <part>]`, `start <app> [--record <dir>]` and `host role: serve <app> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]`; `start --record` and `mcp --record` check the recording directory first, a refusal ending status `3` with nothing spawned or served. No command's ending writes back anything the caller typed, but `caused` carries an app's own messages and fields as their author wrote them, `error` included, scrubbed by the answer's own hidden field names, so an app that writes typed text into a record echoes it. `start` spawns the running binary again as `serve <app> --session <dir>`, with `--record <dir>` after it when it was given one, its streams closed, waits up to 30 s for it to answer, and neither kills nor reaps it.

- The wire (`wire.rs`, crate-private, versioned `v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) is one request line and one reply line per connection: `hello v3` → `ok v3 pid= label= served= idle_expiry_s=`, `stop v3` → `ok v3 stopping`, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` → `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` (sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed`), another version of a known word → `refused version`, anything else → `refused malformed`. Kinds are `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value are percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly. A request is bounded at 16,384 bytes, a lifecycle reply at 128, an answer at 1,048,576 on its JSON line; each read and write at 2 s, a client's read of an answer at 30 s. **What the screen reads crosses it in an answer** — ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask), the snapshot's text and the diff — and an element id and typed text cross in (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); no `NodeId` crosses. Inside the text and the diff an element that states one also reads selected, pressed or invalid — closed words in the text, booleans in a diff node, never an attribute's value as typed: an inventory fact of the ratified crossing, not a further widening (the founder, 2026-10-10), who set the rule with it — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. The MCP surface was that next crossing question: since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the same content crosses to an MCP client in tool results over the `mcp` role's stdio, the request-id echo and the bounds above ratified by the founder with it (2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); the next surface that carries any of it is a new crossing question — since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the operator-driven live cold-agent run carries the stand's screen (element ids, accessible names and control values in snapshot texts and diffs, from this MCP server) on to the model provider, one run, on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» and «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-15). Since 2026-10-12-self-description the command line's stdout and the `mcp` role's stdio also carry the program's own fixed text, held as `'static` data of the one table — the `help` self-description, a session error's remedy and each tool's description with its result fields — riding those ratified carriers, and a changed node's `differs` crosses as a closed set by the rule of 2026-10-10 (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or a new exit still widens. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a shot's pixels cross in band on those carriers — its PNG as base64 inside the answer on the session socket and the command line's stdout, and as an MCP `image` block on the `mcp` role's stdio — screen content and no closed value set, with no new carrier, exit or path argument and the 1,048,576-byte bounds unchanged, a bigger image ending `oversize` / `AnswerTooLarge`: a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-12). Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint a lint's findings cross on those carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` — with no new carrier, exit, path argument, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening; since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts a screen over the snapshot budget crosses them in parts — `snapshot`'s optional `part` (a whole number, 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000) in, one part's text with the closed counts `part` and `parts` out, a part past the last the empty text, a screen within the budget answering whole as before, over MCP a paged answer its JSON line — with no new verb, carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-10-31-select-popup the select list crosses the ratified carriers only as a row's own `bounds` in the snapshot and the diff — `differs` naming `bounds`, a closed set inside the ratified crossing — and as pixels in a `screenshot`, with no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, node key, log field or span; an option's and a group's label leaving as pixels in every shot of an open list is a boundary widening, ratified. Since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the UI graph crosses the ratified carriers — the session socket's `call`, the command line and MCP, as a text block — and rests in a kept check as the `graph` verb's answer: stable ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the declared writes the app authors, the closed flag words `undeclared` and `unconfirmed` and booleans, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`; each snapshot node carries the closed bool `clickable`; no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening.
